approach:
To begin this lesson, show students the Explore task and ask them who they think is correct, Amira or Tama? Show them the numbers on a number line and emphasise how useful this is when rounding numbers because we can see how close the number is to each 10. Discuss which child is correct and how they know. Then together with the class, draw up a set of rules for rounding to 10 with reference to the examples in the Master section. Explain the term approximately, almost equal to, in the context of rounding numbers. Students may have experienced rounding if they have used cash to pay for items in shops.
During Guided Practice, students are using their knowledge of rounding to 10.
formative_assessment:
recognise and count numbers up to and including 80.
Students can use concrete materials to represent numbers in the tens.
Students can draw pictures to represent numbers in the tens on a number line.
Students can use visual tools (such as a number line) to position numbers.
Students can round numbers to the nearest 10.
national_curriculum: Round whole numbers up to 1,000 to the nearest hundred or ten.

objective: round numbers to the nearest 10 and 100.
approach:
To begin this lesson, show students the Explore task and allow them time to discuss who is correct, Meilani or Holly? Talk about what is the same and what is different in what each child is saying. Model rounding on the number line as shown in Master 1. Draw students' attention to how the rounding is written and the 'approximately equal to' sign. Work through Master 1–4 using the key questions to guide students' thoughts. Feedback the 'rules' when rounding to the nearest 100 and 10 and have these on display for students.
During Guided Practice, students are rounding numbers to the nearest 10 and 100.
formative_assessment:
recognise and count numbers up to and including 1000.
Students can use concrete materials to represent numbers in the hundreds.
Students can draw pictures to represent numbers in the hundreds on a number line.
Students can use visual tools (like a number line) to position numbers.
Students can round numbers to the nearest 10 and 100.
national_curriculum: Round whole numbers up to 1,000 to the nearest hundred or ten.

approach:
Mind Challenge
During the mind challenge, students make 3-digit numbers that will round to a specific 3-digit number.
My Maths Journal
During the My My Maths Journal activity, students find examples of when they would round numbers to the nearest 10 or 100. Students should be encouraged to think about situations in real life where rounding would be useful.
Review
Complete this with students as a chapter summary and determine if any of them need extra support.
